_comment: Error codes a document NAMES that no published package exports, EACH WITH ITS REASON.
This file stays short or the documents are wrong. Past twenty entries, that is the sign that
prose is promising a vocabulary nobody is writing — not that the gate is too severe.
SINGLE, AND KEYED BY CODE, because a promise is a fact about the VOCABULARY and not about the
document that happens to mention it. A code named in two documents would, in a per-document
list, give one reason two homes, and two homes drift. That
is the parallel literal table check-vocabulary.py exists to find, so it must not be built inside
it. Precedent: domain-only-vocabularies.json is a side file keyed by name.
TWO KINDS, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS NOT COSMETIC:
`promised` — the project has decided this code will exist; the surface that emits it is not
built. The reason names that surface.
`open`     — prose names a refusal the vocabulary has NEVER declared, and whether it should is
an open product decision. Nobody has promised these. They are questions, and the
reason says so rather than inventing a plan for them.
check-vocabulary.py RETRACTS an entry the day a package exports the code: a promise kept is an
entry to delete, and a stale allowance is the rot these gates exist to find. It cannot retract an
entry nobody names any more — see the gate's header for why that is a note and not a failure.
`named_in` is where the code is named, so a reader can opt that document in without hunting for
it. The gate prints it beside an entry no CHECKED document names, and fails if a checked document
names a code the field leaves out — the field cannot quietly become a lie, though it cannot be
verified against a document nobody checks.
An entry here is not a licence to keep writing a code nobody can emit. It records that a
document names one, with the reason, so the gap is measured instead of discovered.

allow.reason: No BFF exists to mint or expire a token; adr-auth.md is Status: proposed. 401 is served today as api.unauthenticated, which D-069's standing exception makes correct rather than vague.
The pairing surface is adr-auth.md §4, Status: proposed. The four PAIRING_ERROR_CODES that do exist cover polling and ownership, not lifetime.
Traefik's own 5xx, served by a static error service. No Traefik configuration exists in any repository yet, so nothing can emit it.
transport.md §5.7's 413. No service enforces a body limit in the contract's vocabulary — the two that exist inherit Fastify's 1 MiB default and answer with its own error shape, not ours.

OPEN PRODUCT DECISION, not a promise. adr-stream-entitlement.md and context-map.md both name `DATE_INTERRUPTED` as a refusal, and the vocabulary has never declared it. `date.outcome_decision_forbidden` and `watch.date_cancelled` exist; whether an interruption is a third state, a cancellation, or an outcome is undecided, and the entitlement consequence differs in each case. Nobody has promised this code.

OPEN PRODUCT DECISION, not a promise. adr-stream-entitlement.md names `SEAT_EXPIRED`. `SeatHold` has `isHoldExpired` and an expiry instant in core, but no refusal code: an expired hold is currently a state a surface reads, not a refusal it is told. Whether it becomes one is undecided, and the family it would join (watch. or order.) is part of that decision — this entry's own spelling is therefore provisional.

OPEN PRODUCT DECISION, not a promise. adr-stream-entitlement.md and skeptic.md name `PLAN_OPENING_MULTI_SCREEN`, and `watch.concurrent_limit_reached` already refuses the concurrency case. Whether a plan-upgrade prompt is a distinct refusal or a param on that one is undecided; skeptic.md is where the doubt is recorded, which is the opposite of a settled plan.

OPEN PRODUCT DECISION, not a promise. docs/streaming.md names `COMPATIBILITY_WORKER_FAILED`, and there is no `streaming.` family in ERROR_CODES at all — so this entry invents a family as well as a member, and both are provisional. It is not clear the failure of an internal worker should reach a client as a refusal rather than as an unavailability; that is the decision.
